counterfactual_missing_items: No history of allogeneic transplantation or systemic GVHD stigmata such as rash, liver enzyme elevation, or upper-GI involvement
No crypt architectural distortion, granulomas, or chronic transmural inflammation typical of inflammatory bowel disease
No diffuse chemotherapy-related mucosal injury beyond the focal rectosigmoid polypoid lesions; the diagnostic inclusions are not explained by chemotherapy-induced colitis
decisive_items: marked expansion of the lamina propria by a dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate predominantly composed of pale histiocytes with vacuolated cytoplasm admixed with eosinophils, neutrophils, and lymphocytes
The histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains
multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
response.rationale: R3 is the only candidate anchored by pathognomonic raw histology: pale histiocytes containing von Kossa- and PAS-positive basophilic targetoid inclusions, i.e., Michaelis-Gutmann bodies, in an immunosuppressed child with colorectal erosive polypoid lesions. R4 accounts for the maintenance chemotherapy and eroded mucosa but cannot explain the diagnostic inclusions. R1 and R2 rely on nonspecific diarrhea, bleeding, or immunosuppression and lack supporting raw histologic, anatomical, or temporal features; GVHD specifically lacks any transplant or systemic GVHD stigmata.

rejected.why: Chronic hematochezia and loose stools are nonspecific; the raw histology shows histiocytic inclusions and no IBD-specific crypt architectural distortion, granulomas, or transmural inflammation.
There is no allogeneic transplant history or systemic GVHD pattern, and neutropenia/lymphopenia plus a mixed infiltrate are not specific for graft-versus-host disease.
